definitions.definition: ell=max(λ,0), regarded as a natural number (the integer-to-natural conversion λ.toNat). This definition imposes no range condition on λ.
J=Fin(ell+1), identified with the integers i satisfying 0≤i≤ell.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ x^r, with x^0=Id_V. Factorials are the usual products, with 0!=1.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ y^r, with y^0=Id_V.
For i∈J set e_i=Y_i(v)=y^i(v)/i!; the index i denotes its natural value.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(ℂ)
definitions.definition: U_ℤ is generated over ℤ by the divided powers x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r. Its action on V is generated by the operators X_r,Y_r. Operator stability under this algebra means stability under every generator.

inputs.statement: Let p be any prime, K any field of characteristic p, λ an integer with 0≤λ<p, V=V(λ) the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1, and x,y,h its Chevalley operators satisfying hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h. Let v∈V be nonzero with xv=0 and hv=λv. Let U_ℤ be the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. Let M⊆V be any U_ℤ-stable free abelian subgroup with an integer basis also a complex basis of V. The target space is M⊗_ℤ K with the induced x,y,h actions and the Chevalley Lie algebra (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, including characteristic two.

output.statement: For every natural t, h(y^t v)=(ell−2t)y^t v, and for t≥1, x(y^t v)=t(ell−t+1)y^(t−1)v. For 0≤t≤ell, x^t y^t v=t!·(∏_{a=0}^{t−1}(ell−a))v≠0, where the product at t=0 is one and all coefficients are taken in ℂ. For every i∈J, e_i≠0 and h(e_i)=(ell−2i)e_i. The function J→ℂ taking i to ell−2i is injective.

argument.text: H001 gives λ≥0, so (ell:ℤ)=λ. All coefficients in this inference are evaluated in ℂ; in particular ell−2t denotes integer subtraction before casting. Prove the weight identity for all natural t by induction. At t=0 it is hv=ell v. If it holds at t, use hy=yh−2y to obtain h(y^(t+1)v)=y h(y^t v)−2y^(t+1)v=(ell−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. This proves the identity for every t.

produces.statement: For every natural t, h(y^t v)=(ell−2t)y^t v, with coefficients in ℂ.

argument.text: Prove the raising identity for positive natural t by induction. For t=1, xyv=yxv+hv=ell v by H001. Given the formula at positive t, use xy=yx+h and F001 to calculate x y^(t+1)v=y x y^t v+h y^t v=[t(ell−t+1)+ell−2t]y^t v=(t+1)(ell−t)y^t v. These base and step computations prove the claimed formula for every positive t.

produces.statement: For every natural t≥1, x(y^t v)=t(ell−t+1)y^(t−1)v over ℂ.

argument.text: For any natural t≤ell, apply F002 successively t times to get x^t y^t v=t! (∏_(a=0)^(t−1)(ell−a))v. This can also be read as induction starting with x^0 y^0 v=v and multiplying by (t+1)(ell−t) in the next step. At t=0 both products are 1. At 1≤t≤ell all factors 1,...,t and ell,ell−1,...,ell−t+1 are positive integers and have nonzero image in ℂ. Their product is nonzero; multiplying the nonzero v of H001 by a nonzero complex scalar cannot yield zero (multiply by its inverse). Hence the displayed vector is nonzero. Thus y^t v≠0 and division by t! preserves nonvanishing. By D005 each e_i is nonzero for i∈J; complex linearity and F001 give h(e_i)=(ell−2i)e_i. If ell−2i=ell−2j in ℂ, cancellation and 2≠0 give the equality of the complex images of i,j; injectivity of the integer embedding in ℂ gives i=j. This proves the eigenvalue function on J injective, and all clauses of the asserted output.
